explanation:
[EFFECT] Wind speed has a monotonically negative effect: calm conditions (near-zero wind) contribute around zero to slightly positive (+0.08), and as wind increases the contribution falls steadily and continuously, reaching roughly −0.7 at the highest observed speeds. There is no reversal or saturation visible in the range of the data.
[IMPORTANCE] This is a lower-moderate-importance feature with a vertical range of roughly 0.7 log-units, broadly comparable to year and weather situation.
[RECOMMENDATION] Plan your staffing and bike availability primarily around the hour of the day — the evening peak (around 5–6 pm) and the morning shoulder (around 8 am) drive the largest swings in demand — and use temperature as the key weather signal, targeting comfortable mild days (~20–25 °C) for maximum expected ridership and scaling back during cold or very hot spells.
